digest.key_takeaway:

articles.title: Anthropic Prices Its IPO at $83 a Share — the Largest IPO in History Starts Trading Today
articles.summary:
Claude's maker is now the biggest stock market debut in history. Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share on Wednesday 18 November — above its $70 to $78 range — raising about $81.3 billion and valuing the company at roughly $1.5 trillion. Its shares start trading today, Thursday 19 November, on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

articles.title: .NET 11 : ASP.NET Core: Union Type Support, OpenAPI 3.2 by Default and Blazor AI Components
articles.summary: Microsoft has released ASP.NET Core in .NET 11. The update adds C# union type support in JSON bodies, asynchronous validation for Minimal APIs, OpenAPI 3.2 by default, and SignalR authentication refresh. Blazor gains a CacheView component, client-side validation for static SSR forms, opt-in circuit pause for inactive tabs, and experimental AI components. Zstandard compression is on by default. By Almir Vuk

articles.title: AB-210 Exam Guide (2026): Skills, Weights, Format and How to Prepare for Dynamics 365 Sales AI Consultant
articles.summary:
Microsoft's AB-210: Accelerating Sales Pipelines with AI in Dynamics 365 is the exam for the Microsoft Certified: Dynamics 365 Sales AI Consultant Associate certification. It's one of the first role-based exams built around AI agents rather than classic CRM configuration, so many familiar study resources don't fully cover it yet.

This guide covers what the exam measures, how it's weighted, which topics deserve the most attention, and how to prepare efficiently. At the end, you'll find a set of AB-210 practice tests I created, currently free with a coupon.

articles.title: I Asked a Local Vision Model 36 Questions About GTA VI. One Answer Broke the Contract.

Gemma 3 returned "blue" for a question that accepted only yes, no, or unclear.

The answer was semantically close. It was still unusable in code.

articles.title: AI Made Coding Cheaper. Why Are Client Projects Still Expensive? (An Agency View)
articles.summary: TL;DR: Clients ask us some version of this a lot now: "If AI writes the code now, why does the project still cost what it costs?" It's a fair question, and the honest answer is that typing code was never most of the bill. AI made the first draft cheap. It did very little for discovery, integration, data, verification, security and running the thing afterwards, and it made one of those (review) more important. Below is an agency's view of where the time goes, a concrete example of a "done in five minutes" feature that took much longer, and what clients can do to make projects cheaper for real.

articles.title: Discord Rewrites Desktop and Mobile Clients in Rust Using Zed's GPU-Accelerated Rendering Framework
articles.summary: Discord’s CTO Stanislav Vishnevskiy recently announced rewriting its desktop and mobile clients in Rust, moving away from Electron and React Native. The project eliminates layers of abstraction to directly leverage the device’s GPU, native mobile views, and a Rust core shared across platforms. Early results hint at a significant reduction in RAM usage and boot time for chat, voice, and streaming. By Bruno Couriol
